0.headline: CBA Posts Record A$30.2B Operating Income in FY26
0.body: Cash operating income rose to A$30.2B, up from ~A$22B five years ago, driven by the NII engine at 84.7% of revenue. The franchise demonstrated durability through rate cycles, compounding income at ~6% CAGR since FY21.

1.headline: Business Banking Leads Group at +11% NPAT
1.body: Business Banking delivered 11% NPAT growth on disciplined volume growth and repricing, offsetting NZ's 7% decline on macro headwinds. Retail held firm despite LIE up 39% from an ultra-low base.

2.headline: NII Commands 84.7% of Revenue Amid Margin Pressure
2.body: NII of A$25.6B dominates the revenue mix at 84.7%, an unusually high share versus global peers, while other income of A$4.6B covers fees, trading and insurance. Structural NIM pressure from deposit repricing remains the key watch item.
2.pull_quote: 84.7% NII share — highest among major banks

3.headline: Business Banking NIM at 3.39% Towers Over Group Average
3.body: Business Banking's 3.39% NIM leads the group's 2.05% by 134bps, reflecting disciplined SME repricing and lower deposit competition. Retail NIM faces ongoing fixed-rate roll-off drag, while NZ margins are compressed by competition and provisioning.

4.headline: CTI Tightens 20bps to 45.5% as Productivity Gains Show
4.body: Opex of A$13.8B against A$30.2B income delivers a 45.5% CTI, improving 20bps year-on-year, with pre-provision profit at a record A$16.5B. Technology and compliance remain the largest cost drivers but the productivity overlay is working.
4.pull_quote: 45.5% CTI — record pre-provision profit of A$16.5B

5.headline: CBA's ~20x PE Premium Tests Patience at Cycle Peak
5.body: CBA trades at ~20x forward earnings versus peers at 13-15x, supported by earnings quality, franchise dominance and a 505c DPS at a 78% payout ratio. NIM headwinds and rising credit costs raise questions about whether that premium is fully earned.
5.pull_quote: ~20x PE — can the franchise premium hold?

6.headline: ROE Rises 50bps to 14.0% as CBA Reaffirms Quality Tag
6.body: Cash NPAT of A$11.0B, ROE of 14.0% (+50bps), EPS of 656.9c and DPS of 505c confirm CBA as Australia's highest-returning major bank. CET1 at 12.0% (-30bps) stays comfortably above APRA's 11.25% unquestionably strong benchmark.
